presets.label: GPT-2 small (124M)
presets.summary: The GPT-2 small recipe: context 1,024, QKV biases, and an output head tied to the token embedding. Its logits match OpenAI's released 124M weights.

presets.label: Qwen3-0.6B, as released
presets.summary: Qwen3-0.6B base with the tied output head of the released checkpoint. The recipe's untied head is overridden here to show the released architecture.

presets.label: Book chapter 5 (162M)
presets.summary: The book's chapter-5 model: GPT-2 small's 12 layers × 768, but with context 256, an untied output head and no QKV biases. It uses the explicit attention kernel, so the attention-weight dropout and the T × T score matrix appear here.

presets.label: TinyStories (51M)
presets.summary: The model this repo trained for 17.5 hours on TinyStories: the GPT-2 block design scaled down to 8 layers × 512.

presets.label: GPT-2 medium (355M)
presets.summary: OpenAI's GPT-2 medium (24 layers × 1,024) as chapter 7 fine-tunes it on Alpaca-style instructions.

presets.label: Qwen3-0.6B, explicit attention
presets.summary: The released Qwen3-0.6B with `attn_impl: explicit`, the book's code path. Attention's scores, causal mask, scaling, softmax and weighted sum appear as separate steps instead of one fused `scaled_dot_product_attention` call. The two paths compute the same result.

presets.label: Qwen3-0.6B, untied head
presets.summary: Qwen3-0.6B as this repo's continued-pretraining and SFT recipes train it, with a separate output head as the book's chapters 6 and 8 train it. The second 151,936 × 1,024 matrix adds 155,582,464 parameters.

presets.label: Smoke test (3M)
presets.summary: The CPU execution check: 2 layers × 32. Almost every parameter is in the embedding and the output head, because the 50,257-token vocabulary stays full size while everything else shrinks.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.title: GPT model
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.text:
Turns token IDs into next-token logits. A token embedding and a learned position embedding are added together, the sum passes through `n_layers` identical transformer blocks, and a final LayerNorm and a linear head give one score per vocabulary entry at every position.

The logits at position t predict token t + 1. Causal masking inside each attention layer stops position t from seeing later tokens.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.title: GPT-2 transformer block
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.text:
Two sublayers, each pre-normalized and wrapped in a residual connection: `x = x + drop(att(norm1(x)))`, then `x = x + drop(ff(norm2(x)))`. The additions aren't modules: they're the `add` steps, the `x = x + shortcut` lines in the code below.

The residual stream keeps the same width from the first block to the last. Each sublayer reads a normalized copy and writes back an update.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.title: Causal multi-head attention
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text:
Queries, keys and values come from three separate linear maps. Each is split into `n_heads` heads of width `emb_dim / n_heads`. Every head scores each query against every earlier key with `Q Kᵀ / √head_dim`; a causal mask sets later positions to −∞ before the softmax. The weighted sum of values goes back through `out_proj`.

The split into heads is a reshape and a transpose: the `view` and `transpose` steps, not a module. With `attn_impl: sdpa`, PyTorch's fused kernel does the scoring without materializing the T × T matrix; the explicit path builds it and applies dropout to it.

The `mask` buffer is `context_length × context_length` and persistent, so it is saved in every checkpoint. Making it non-persistent is backlog item A7.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.LayerNorm.title: LayerNorm
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.LayerNorm.text: For each token, subtracts the mean across the embedding dimension, divides by the standard deviation (with eps 1e-5), then applies a learned per-channel `scale` and `shift`. Two vectors of width `emb_dim`.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.GELU.title: GELU (tanh approximation)
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.GELU.text: A smooth ReLU: `0.5 x (1 + tanh(√(2/π) (x + 0.044715 x³)))`, the approximation GPT-2 used. It has no parameters; its buffer is the constant √(2/π), kept so it isn't rebuilt every call.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.title: GPT-2 feed-forward network
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.text: Applied to each token independently: expand from `emb_dim` to 4 × `emb_dim`, apply GELU, project back. About two thirds of each block's parameters are here.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.title: Qwen3 model
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text:
The same outline as GPT: embed, run `n_layers` blocks, normalize, project to the vocabulary. But there's no position embedding. Position enters inside attention instead, by rotating queries and keys (RoPE), and the rotation tables `cos` and `sin` are the buffers on this model, computed once for all `context_length` positions.

The causal mask is built once here and passed to every block, along with the RoPE tables. That's why each block takes `(x, mask, cos, sin)` rather than just `x`.

Nothing is added to the token embedding, unlike GPT-2's `tok_emb + pos_emb`. `x` starts as `tok_emb`'s output, and `mask`, `cos` and `sin` travel beside it as separate arguments that only attention reads. With `attn_impl: sdpa`, `is_causal=True` masks inside the kernel, so not even attention reads `mask`.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Transform.title: Qwen3 transformer block
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Transform.text:
The same pre-norm residual pattern as GPT-2: `x = x + att(norm1(x))`, then `x = x + ff(norm2(x))`. Each piece differs: RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, grouped-query attention with RoPE, SwiGLU instead of GELU, and no dropout anywhere.

The attention also returns a key/value cache for fast decoding. This repo's generation doesn't use it yet.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.title: Grouped-query attention with RoPE and QK-norm
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text:
There are 16 query heads but only 8 key/value heads. Each K/V head is shared by a group of 2 query heads, via `repeat_interleave`, which halves the K and V projections and the KV cache. Compare the output widths: `W_query` produces 16 × 128 = 2,048 channels, while `W_key` and `W_value` produce 8 × 128 = 1,024.

`head_dim` is 128 and set independently of `emb_dim`, so the heads together are wider (2,048) than the residual stream (1,024); `out_proj` maps back down.

After splitting into heads, queries and keys are RMS-normalized per head (QK-norm, which keeps attention logits in range), then rotated by RoPE. Rotating q and k by an angle proportional to their position makes their dot product depend on the distance between them. RoPE is a function, `apply_rope`, not a module. It appears twice, once for the queries and once for the keys, with its steps inside.

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.RMSNorm.title: RMSNorm
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.RMSNorm.text: Divides each vector by its root-mean-square (with eps 1e-6) and applies a learned per-channel `scale`. Unlike LayerNorm it neither subtracts the mean nor adds a shift: one vector instead of two, and slightly less work. It computes in float32 whatever the input type.

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.title: SwiGLU feed-forward network
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.text: `fc3(silu(fc1(x)) * fc2(x))`. Two parallel projections up to `hidden_dim` (3,072): one goes through SiLU and acts as a gate on the other, multiplied element by element; then `fc3` projects back. Three matrices rather than GPT-2's two, and no biases. The multiply is the `mul` step, not a module.

torch.nn.Embedding.title: Embedding
torch.nn.Embedding.text: A lookup table: row i of `weight` is the vector for index i. No arithmetic happens: the backward pass gives a nonzero gradient only to the rows that were looked up.

torch.nn.Linear.title: Linear
torch.nn.Linear.text: `y = x Wᵀ + b`, applied to the last dimension. `weight` is stored as `[out, in]`, which is why its shape reads backwards against the arrow.

torch.nn.Dropout.title: Dropout
torch.nn.Dropout.text: During training, zeroes each value with probability `drop_rate` and scales the rest by 1 / (1 − p). It does nothing in evaluation mode. In this repo, recipes that start from released GPT-2 weights default to a rate of 0, as chapter 7 does.

torch.nn.Sequential.title: Sequential
torch.nn.Sequential.text: Calls its children in order, passing each output to the next. It holds no parameters of its own.

llm_training.model.qwen3.rope.apply_rope.title: Rotary position embedding (RoPE)
llm_training.model.qwen3.rope.apply_rope.text:
Rotates each query or key vector by an angle proportional to its position, so that the dot product of a query at position m and a key at position n depends only on m − n. Channel i is paired with channel i + 64 (the split-halves layout): `x · cos + (−x₂, x₁) · sin` rotates every pair by its own angle.

The angles come from the `cos` and `sin` tables on the model, `[context_length, head_dim]`, computed once when the model is built. Each call slices the first T rows (the `getitem` steps that use `cos` and `sin`) and adds two size-1 dimensions, so one table broadcasts over the batch and all heads. RoPE has no parameters: positions enter only through these fixed rotations.

torch.Tensor.__getitem__.title: Index or slice
torch.Tensor.__getitem__.text: `x[...]` selects part of a tensor. A slice such as `x[..., :64]` or `cos[:T]` is a view of the same memory, so nothing is copied. `None` in the index, as in `mask[None, None]`, adds a size-1 dimension so the tensor broadcasts.

torch.Tensor.add.title: Add
torch.Tensor.add.text: Element-wise addition, broadcasting size-1 dimensions. In a block, `x + shortcut` is the residual connection: the sublayer's output is added to its input, so each sublayer writes an update into the residual stream instead of replacing it.

torch.Tensor.bool.title: Convert to boolean
torch.Tensor.bool.text: Turns the stored 0/1 mask into True/False, the form `masked_fill` takes.

torch.Tensor.div.title: Divide
torch.Tensor.div.text: Element-wise division, broadcasting. LayerNorm divides by the standard deviation. Attention divides the scores by √head_dim, which keeps them from growing with the head width and saturating the softmax.

torch.Tensor.masked_fill.title: Mask
torch.Tensor.masked_fill.text: Returns a copy with a value written wherever a boolean mask is True. Attention writes −∞ into the scores of later positions, so the softmax gives them a weight of exactly 0.

torch.Tensor.masked_fill_.title: Mask, in place
torch.Tensor.masked_fill_.text: Writes a value wherever a boolean mask is True; the trailing underscore means it changes the tensor in place. Attention writes −∞ into the scores of later positions, so the softmax gives them a weight of exactly 0.

torch.Tensor.matmul.title: Matrix multiply
torch.Tensor.matmul.text: `@`: a matrix product over the last two dimensions, batched over the others. `queries @ keys.transpose(2, 3)` scores every query against every key, a `[T, T]` matrix per head; `weights @ values` mixes the values by those weights.

torch.Tensor.mean.title: Mean
torch.Tensor.mean.text: The average over a dimension. `keepdim=True` keeps that dimension with size 1, so the result broadcasts back against the input.

torch.Tensor.mul.title: Multiply
torch.Tensor.mul.text: Element-wise multiplication, broadcasting. It applies the norms' learned `scale`, the SwiGLU gate, RoPE's `cos` and `sin` factors, and GELU's constants.

torch.Tensor.neg.title: Negate
torch.Tensor.neg.text: Flips the sign: RoPE's `−x₂`, the first half of the rotated vector.

torch.Tensor.pow.title: Power
torch.Tensor.pow.text: Element-wise power. RMSNorm squares each channel, `x.pow(2)`, before averaging.

torch.Tensor.repeat_interleave.title: Repeat each head
torch.Tensor.repeat_interleave.text: Repeats each slice along a dimension in place: with 2 repeats on the head dimension, heads [a, b] become [a, a, b, b]. Grouped-query attention uses it so each key/value head lines up with every query head in its group.

torch.Tensor.reshape.title: Reshape
torch.Tensor.reshape.text: Same values in a new shape. Unlike `view` it copies when the memory layout requires it, as after a `transpose`. Here it joins the heads back into one vector per token.

torch.Tensor.sub.title: Subtract
torch.Tensor.sub.text: Element-wise subtraction, broadcasting. LayerNorm subtracts each token's mean.

torch.Tensor.to.title: Convert dtype
torch.Tensor.to.text: Casts to another dtype. RMSNorm and RoPE compute in float32 and cast back to the input's type; in this repo's float32 models both casts return the tensor unchanged. They matter when the model runs in bfloat16.

torch.Tensor.transpose.title: Swap two dimensions
torch.Tensor.transpose.text: Swaps two dimensions without copying. After the split into heads, `transpose(1, 2)` moves heads ahead of tokens, so each head is its own `[T, head_dim]` matrix for the batched matrix products; afterwards it moves them back.

torch.Tensor.unsqueeze.title: Add a dimension
torch.Tensor.unsqueeze.text: Inserts a size-1 dimension so a tensor broadcasts against a larger one: RoPE's `[T, head_dim]` tables become `[1, 1, T, head_dim]`, shared by every sequence and head.

torch.Tensor.var.title: Variance
torch.Tensor.var.text: The variance over a dimension. `unbiased=False` divides by n rather than n − 1, as LayerNorm is defined.

torch.Tensor.view.title: View with a new shape
torch.Tensor.view.text: The same memory read with a new shape; nothing is copied. `view(B, T, heads, head_dim)` splits each token's vector into heads.

torch.arange.title: Positions 0 to T − 1
torch.arange.text: The position indices 0, 1, …, T − 1, which select rows of the position-embedding table.

torch.cat.title: Concatenate
torch.cat.text: Joins tensors along a dimension. RoPE builds `(−x₂, x₁)`, each pair's partner swapped and one sign flipped, which is the rotation's sine term.

torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_a.title: Fused attention
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_a.text:
`softmax(Q Kᵀ / √head_dim + mask) V` in one call: scores, scaling, causal mask, softmax and the weighted sum of values, without storing the `[T, T]` score matrix. With `is_causal=True` the kernel applies the causal mask itself. Qwen3's model still builds a mask (its `ones`, `triu` and `getitem` steps) and passes it to every block, but on this path only cached decoding reads it.

The explicit path computes the same thing as separate steps: `matmul`, `masked_fill`, `div`, `softmax` and `matmul` again. The presets with `attn_impl: explicit` show them.

torch.nn.functional.silu.title: SiLU
torch.nn.functional.silu.text: `x · sigmoid(x)`, a smooth ReLU. In SwiGLU it turns the `fc1` branch into a gate that scales the `fc2` branch.

torch.ones.title: Tensor of ones
torch.ones.text: A `[T, T]` matrix of True values, the starting point for the causal mask.

torch.rsqrt.title: Reciprocal square root
torch.rsqrt.text: `1 / √x` in one operation. RMSNorm multiplies by it rather than dividing by the root mean square.

torch.softmax.title: Softmax
torch.softmax.text: Turns each row of scores into weights that are positive and sum to 1. Positions masked to −∞ get exactly 0.

torch.tanh.title: tanh
torch.tanh.text: The hyperbolic tangent in GELU's approximation.

torch.triu.title: Upper triangle
torch.triu.text: Keeps the entries above the diagonal (`diagonal=1`) and clears the rest. From a matrix of ones, that leaves True exactly at the later positions each token must not attend to.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: RoPE rotation table (cosines)
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text:
RoPE's cosines. Row m holds cos(m · θ⁻²ⁱᐟ¹²⁸) for each of the 64 channel pairs i, written twice (columns i and i + 64) to match the split-halves layout. `compute_rope_params` builds it once, for every position up to `context_length`, when the model is built.

Each `apply_rope` call takes the first T rows and multiplies the queries or keys by them: the `x · cos` half of the rotation.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: RoPE rotation table (sines)
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text: RoPE's sines, laid out like `cos`. Each `apply_rope` call takes the first T rows and multiplies them by the swapped copy `(−x₂, x₁)`: the `rotated · sin` half of the rotation.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Causal mask
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: A `context_length × context_length` matrix of ones above the diagonal: the later positions each token must not see. The explicit attention path takes the top-left T × T, converts it to boolean and fills those scores with −∞. With `attn_impl: sdpa` the kernel's `is_causal=True` applies the mask itself and this buffer isn't read.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.GELU._sqr.label: Constant √(2/π)
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.GELU._sqr.text: The constant √(2/π) ≈ 0.798 in GELU's tanh approximation, stored once so it isn't rebuilt on every call.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.scaled_dot_product_attention(: Fused attention: scores, mask, softmax, weighted sum

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.RMSNorm.x * torch.rsqrt(variance + self.eps): Divide by the root mean square
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.RMSNorm.norm_x.to(input_dtype): Cast back to the input dtype

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.keys.repeat_interleave(: Share each key head with its query group
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.values.repeat_interleave(: Share each value head with its query group
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.scaled_dot_product_attention(: Fused attention: scores, mask, softmax, weighted sum

llm_training.model.qwen3.rope.apply_rope.x_rotated.to(dtype: Cast back to the input dtype

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.t.label: Token embedding
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.t.text: One learned vector per vocabulary entry: 50,257 rows of width `emb_dim`.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.p.label: Position embedding, learned
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.p.text: One learned vector per position, up to `context_length`. It's looked up with `arange(T)`, so its input has no batch dimension; broadcasting adds the same position vectors to every sequence.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.d.label: Embedding dropout
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.d.text: Dropout on the summed token and position embeddings.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.t.label: Transformer blocks
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.t.text: `n_layers` blocks with identical structure and separate weights, in an `nn.Sequential`.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.f.label: Final norm
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.f.text: One last normalization of the residual stream before the vocabulary projection.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.o.label: LM head: logits over the vocabulary
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.GPTModel.o.text: Projects each position to one logit per vocabulary entry. With `tie_embeddings`, it reuses the token embedding matrix (GPT-2 does), saving `vocab × emb_dim` parameters; the book's chapter-5 model keeps a separate matrix.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.label: Pre-attention norm
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.text: Normalizes the attention sublayer's input; the residual path itself stays unnormalized.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.label: Causal self-attention
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.text: Mixes information between positions: the only place one token sees another.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.label: Residual dropout
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.text: Called twice per block, after attention and after the feed-forward network, before each residual add. One module serves both because dropout has no parameters.

llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.label: Feed-forward network (MLP)
llm_training.model.gpt2.model.Transforme.text: Processes each position on its own, with no mixing between tokens.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Query projection
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: What each position is looking for.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Key projection
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: What each position offers to be matched against.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Value projection
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: What each position contributes when it's attended to.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Attention dropout
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: Dropout on the attention weights. Its input is the full `[B, heads, T, T]` matrix, which is why explicit attention's memory grows with the square of the context.

llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.label: Output projection
llm_training.model.gpt2.attention.MultiH.text: Mixes the concatenated head outputs back into the residual stream.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.label: Expand to 4 × emb_dim
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.text: The first linear layer widens each token's vector four times, from `emb_dim` to 4 × `emb_dim`: 3,072 channels in GPT-2 small.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.label: GELU activation
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.text: The nonlinearity between the two linear layers. Without it the pair would collapse into a single linear map.

llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.label: Project back to emb_dim
llm_training.model.gpt2.layers.FeedForwa.text: The second linear layer maps the 4 × `emb_dim` channels back to `emb_dim`, the width of the residual stream.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: Token embedding
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text: 151,936 rows of width 1,024: about a quarter of the released model's parameters.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: Transformer blocks
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text: 28 blocks with identical structure and separate weights. They're in an `nn.ModuleList` that the forward loop iterates, so the list itself is never called and has no row.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: Final norm
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text: One last RMSNorm before the vocabulary projection.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.label: LM head: logits over the vocabulary
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Qwen3Mode.text: Projects to 151,936 logits. The released model ties it to `tok_emb`; this repo's fine-tuning recipes train a separate copy, as the book does.

llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Transform.label: Grouped-query self-attention
llm_training.model.qwen3.model.Transform.text: Grouped-query attention: where tokens exchange information, and where position (RoPE) enters the model.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: Query projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: 16 heads × 128 = 2,048 outputs: wider than the 1,024-wide residual stream.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: Key projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: Only 8 heads × 128 = 1,024 outputs: each key head serves two query heads. (That this equals `emb_dim` is a coincidence.)

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: Value projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: 8 value heads, shared the same way as the keys.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: QK-norm, queries
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: RMSNorm over each query head's 128 channels. Its input is already split into heads: `[B, 16, T, 128]`.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: QK-norm, keys
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: RMSNorm over each key head: `[B, 8, T, 128]`, half the heads of the queries.

llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.label: Output projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.attention.Group.text: 2,048 concatenated head channels back down to the 1,024-wide residual stream.

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.label: Gate projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.text: The gate branch: its output goes through SiLU.

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.label: Up projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.text: The value branch, multiplied by the gate.

llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.label: Down projection
llm_training.model.qwen3.layers.FeedForw.text: Projects the gated 3,072 channels back to 1,024.
